Bhagavad Gita, Chapter 4, Verse 17

“One must understand the nature of action, the nature of wrong action, and also the nature of inaction. The way of action is deep and hard to see.”

Three categories rather than two, and Krishna calls the terrain gahana — deep, tangled, overgrown. The honesty about its difficulty is itself part of the teaching.
